## Meet Yassamin
Yassamin Ansari served as the Vice Mayor of Phoenix and was the youngest woman ever elected to the Phoenix City Council, representing one of the most diverse districts in the fifth-largest and fastest growing city in the country.
The proud daughter of immigrants and graduate of Stanford and Cambridge universities, Yassamin led the charge to pass the city’s landmark Climate Action Plan, has fought for the protection of reproductive rights, and secured millions in free tuition for students pursuing community college and good jobs in the trades.
Mayor Kate Gallego Endorses Yassamin Ansari for Congress
Phoenix Mayor Kate Gallego announced her support for Yassamin Ansari in the race for Arizona’s Third Congressional District.
October 30, 2024
Members of House Democratic Leadership Endorse Yassamin Ansari for Congress
Members of House Democratic Leadership announced their support for Yassamin Ansari in the race for Arizona’s Third Congressional District.

Representative Greg Stanton announced his support for Yassamin Ansari in the race for Arizona’s Third Congressional District.

Congressional Progressive Caucus PAC Endorses Yassamin Ansari for Congress

pages.title: Issues & Policy - Yassamin for Congress
pages.text:
## Issues & Policy
As a Councilwoman, Yassamin has championed housing affordability, climate action, reproductive freedom, worker’s rights, and education – with proven results.
Fighting for working families is central as to why Yassamin ran for city council in the first place – and will remain so as she takes her fight to Congress.
Women’s rights and their bodily autonomy have been under attack across the United States and in Arizona.
When the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade, Yassamin passed an ordinance to direct the Phoenix Police Department to make harsh state abortion laws its lowest priority for enforcement to protect doctors, nurses, pharmacists and patients from arrest for practicing and receiving basic healthcare. Yassamin believes that women’s access to reproductive healthcare is a vital tool for empowering women’s health, autonomy, and financial choice.
In Congress, she will support policies that:
- Protect a woman’s right to choose by codifying Roe v. Wade
- Support for the Equal Rights Amendment
- Fund the Violence Against Women Act
Our democracy is under attack. We must not take it for granted and do everything to fight against the forces trying to disenfranchise the voices of everyday Americans. As the daughter of immigrants who were displaced by persecution and a brutal theocratic and authoritarian regime, protecting democracy is personal to Yassamin.
To restore and strengthen our democracy, Yassamin will support:
- The Freedom to Vote Act, which ends partisan gerrymandering, cracks down on dark money in politics, establishes automatic voter registration, and combats voter suppression.
- The John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act, which would restore the strength of the Voting Rights Act of 1965.
- Ending the Jim Crow-era filibuster and expanding the U.S. Supreme Court, so that our democracy can work for everyday people, not just the powerful and rich.
- Prohibit members of Congress from stock trading, so that those who govern aren’t able to use private information to get wealthy
- Curb the revolving door in Washington by creating new regulations to prevent former Members of Congress from becoming lobbyists.
The climate crisis is the defining issue of our time. As a climate policy expert, Yassamin has pushed for international solutions to climate change at the United Nations and led bold efforts to clean up our air and water in Phoenix.
She passed the city’s landmark Climate Action Plan, created the first Office of Heat Response and Mitigation in the nation, and built a coalition on the city council to unanimously pass the city’s ambitious Transportation Electrification Action Plan, ushering in a clean energy future for Phoenix. She also spearheaded a plan to electrify Phoenix’s bus fleet by 2040, reducing our carbon emissions and improving air quality in the city.
In Congress, Yassamin will lead and support policies that:
- Accelerate the transition from fossil fuels to clean, renewable energy
- Increase investment into building resilience to climate impacts
- Work directly with FEMA to declare heat as a natural disaster to unlock resource management capabilities to support our district
- Stand up to Big Oil who have tried to stagnate and roll back President Biden’s climate policies, including the Bipartisan Infrastructure Bill and the Inflation Reduction Act
- Create new jobs that will help grow a greener economy and lead efforts for a “just transition” for the millions of workers currently employed in the fossil fuel, manufacturing and automotive industries
- Lead to a Green New Deal that protects working families, invests in high wage union jobs, and keeps our cities livable
In Arizona and around the country, we’re facing a historic housing shortage – Yassamin is a pro-housing champion with a record of getting things done to lower rent and housing costs. Experts estimate that Arizona is 270,000 homes short of what we need to keep up with our growing population. This directly contributes to high housing costs, our recent spike in homelessness, and will have detrimental effects to our economy if we don’t take bold action. Building more housing so we have the supply we need will be a top priority for Yassamin in Congress.
On the Phoenix City Council, Yassamin worked to prioritize housing solutions and has delivered for us by directing over $120 million in American Rescue Plan Act funding to projects supporting affordable housing and homelessness including rental assistance which has helped over 19,000 families, helping approve a record number of new housing units, and by leading the effort to legalize casitas.
In Congress, Yassamin will continue this work by supporting policies that:
- Pass historic levels of funding to build affordable housing and increase the supply of Housing Choice Vouchers
- Work with local communities to make it easier to build all types of housing through comprehensive zoning reform
- Prevent evictions by helping families remain in their housing and end source of income discrimination
- Incentivize social housing projects that house a mixture of income levels
- Assist municipalities as they work to tackle homelessness with funding for wraparound services, shelters, and transitional housing
Our LGBTQIA+ community has spent decades tirelessly fighting for their rights but we have seen a surge in anti-LGBTQIA+ laws in recent years. Yassamin will continue to fight for a world strengthened by our diversity, where our laws and society treat all people equally. As a Phoenix City Councilwoman, Yassamin was a relentless advocate for our LGBTQ+ community. She hosted an annual Pride On The Block festival in downtown Phoenix, most recently in November 2023 during Trans Visibility Week, to raise funds for organizations like One N’ Ten and the Southwest Center for HIV & Aids, and directed millions in investments to nonprofit organizations serving this community. In Congress, she will support:
- The Equality Act, which prohibits discrimination in housing, employments and public accommodations based on sexual orientation and gender identity
- Respect for Marriage Act, which ensures and protects marriage equality
- Banning Conversion therapy on LGBTQ+ folks, especially minors
- Telling the U.S. Census Bureau to count LGBTQ+ people
Labor unions uplift the middle class and help the working class build economic power. Strengthening unions and workers’ rights is fundamental to building an equitable economy. That’s why as a Councilwoman and Vice Mayor, Yassamin helped lead the charge to raise wages for thousands of city employees – from firefighters and police officers to bus drivers and librarians – and voted to pass a historic prevailing wage ordinance in the City of Phoenix. In March 2024, she led the charge to pass Phoenix’s Worker Heat Safety Ordinance, a first of its kind policy that will help protect 10,000 outdoor workers from extreme summer heat.
Yassamin believes that collective bargaining is a vital mechanism for economic progress and will support the following policies in Congress:
- Fund enforcement mechanisms of labor laws
- Protect the Right to Organize (PRO) Act
- Promote prevailing wage laws established by the Davis-Bacon Act
- Ensure Community Workforce Agreements
Many Arizonans are feeling left behind in today’s economy with their wages not keeping up with rising living and healthcare costs. We need to prioritize building an economy that benefits everyone. We need to replace our trickle-down economy with one that focuses on strengthening the middle class and expanding economic mobility.
To build an economy for all, Yassamin believes economic growth should be built on the foundation of the following principles and policies:
- Increase the federal minimum wage
- Strengthen worker power by supporting workers’ rights, collective bargaining and organizing
- Stand up to greedy corporate interests and crack down on price gouging to lower costs for working families
- Support a green, sustainable and modernized economy that in turn creates well-paying jobs of the future
- Lower the cost of healthcare, housing, and childcare through permanently expanding the Child Tax Credit and Earned Income Tax Credit
- Keep taxes low for working families and senior citizens, while ensuring the wealthy also pay their fair share to invest in vital public services
- Prevent corporate monopolies and mergers that give too much control to too few and harm consumers
- End homelessness through investments in accessible, affordable housing
- Support small businesses by expanding resources for small business owners and investing in our communities
- Tax the wealthy. It’s time for a comprehensive tax system that benefits working people and ensures the top 1%, Wall Street, and large corporations pay their fair share.
- Lead the way in the blockchain and crypto innovation. By leading and establishing guidelines to innovate, we can make sure we protect consumers and create more equitable access for all.
Raised by immigrant parents, Yassamin fully understands the value our immigrant communities bring to our nation’s culture, economy, and spirit. Yassamin has always worked to support immigrant communities, and created Phoenix’s first Office of Refugee Support to help families access employment, healthcare, and housing services. Migrant families should no longer be treated as political pawns and they deserve comprehensive immigration reform. While DACA needs continued support, it is a product of years of inaction and congressional gridlock. We need holistic and comprehensive immigration reform now.
In Congress, Yassamin will support:
- The American Dream and Promise Act, the American Families United Act, the Dignity for Detained Immigrants Act, and the New Deal for New Americans Act.
- Making legal counsel for refugees and immigrants more accessible
Access to education is a vital tool for Americans to empower themselves and their communities, but Arizonans face high barriers to entry with the quality and costs of education. On the Phoenix City Council, Yassamin worked to provide young people with the opportunity to pursue higher education by establishing the Phoenix Promise – a scholarship program that supports 800 low-income students in pursuing a community college education. She will continue to advocate for education in Congress by supporting policies that:
- Support our public schools through increased funding for students and teachers to meet their full potential
- Forgive student loan debt so that younger generations can use their education to work towards economic freedom
- Expanding rural broadband access for students and teachers
## Policy Plans
Climate Plan for a Greener, Safer Future
Glendale, Guadalupe, and Phoenix are on the front lines of climate change, extreme heat, and water scarcity, and it’s up to our generation of leaders to take bold action to save lives and ensure a safe and healthy quality life for the decades to come.
July 12, 2024
Federal Economic Prosperity Plan: Lowering Costs for Working Families
It is imperative that our leaders and elected officials work to ensure that the current rising cost of living for our working families goes down to ensure that we can provide economic stability and financial freedom.
June 28, 2024
Federal Economic Prosperity Plan: Small Business Advancement
In our first plan, we address the ways in which our minority-owned small businesses face barriers to their economic success, and the ways in which we can advocate for systemic change from the top down to ensure that everyone has access to the same resources.
June 28, 2024
Reproductive Rights & Women’s Health Policy Plan 2024
Yassamin is dedicated to ensuring that we stop rolling back the clocks on reproductive healthcare, and enshrine it as a fundamental right once and for all.
April 15, 2024
Housing & Homelessness Policy Plan 2024
Universal access to safe, stable,
and affordable housing is the cornerstone of a thriving community—one where everyone can live with dignity.
February 16, 2024

## Meet Yassamin
Congresswoman Yassamin Ansari represents Arizona’s Third Congressional District – one of the most diverse communities in the country and home to Phoenix, the fifth-largest city in America. She is the youngest woman in the 119th Congress and serves as Democratic Freshman Class President.
In her first term, Yassamin has taken on corruption in Washington and been a fearless voice against Donald Trump and his authoritarian agenda. She’s worked to rein in ICE and protect immigrant communities, defend reproductive freedom, and advance a bold agenda to lower costs for Arizonans. On the powerful House Oversight Committee, she has taken on some of the most powerful figures in the country – fighting to hold abusers and their enablers accountable and demand justice for survivors in the Epstein case.
Congresswomen Rashida Tlaib, Yassamin Ansari denounce ‘immoral’ Iran war
“In the past six months since Donald Trump started his illegal war in Iran, 120 children died after a US military strike hit their school, 18 American servicemembers have been killed, Americans have endured record high gas costs, and Donald Trump and his sons have profited endlessly from investing in

“He is absolutely insane, out of touch & evil. A conman who’s grifted his way to the presidency and is now actively stealing from us every day says that American service members at sea ‘have been deployed for not nearly long enough.”

## Yassamin's platform
In Congress, Yassamin is standing up fiercely to the corrupt and authoritarian Trump administration. She is fighting for working families as a champion for Medicare for All, housing and childcare affordability, AI security, climate action and public education – with proven results.
As Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus’s Lowering Costs Task Force, Yassamin is dedicated to passing bold, commonsense policies to bring down the cost of living and make the American Dream a reality for all Americans.
Yassamin believes Congress must pass Medicare for All before more hardworking Americans are crushed by medical debt and surprise bills. We must build more affordable housing , provide free childcare to working families, and expand essential programs like SNAP and the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP).
She also supports raising the federal minimum wage for the first time in nearly two decades – to a liveable wage of $25/hour.
Yassamin believes we must abolish and prosecute ICE, Stephen Miller, and all those responsible for its sadistic mass deportation agenda, full stop.
In the 119th Congress, she introduced the Fund Schools, Not ICE Act, which would transfer over $39 billion in unobligated ICE funding to Title I grants for local school districts; the Drain ICE Act, which eliminates $75 billion in ICE funding appropriated in the so-called One Big Beautiful Bill Act; the Studying Disastrous Impacts of Mass Deportations Act, which conducts a study on the long-term economic impacts of Trump’s immigration policies; and the Stop Inhumane Conditions in ICE Detention Act, which mandates reporting requirements about detainees in immigration detention facilities.
To date, she has conducted over 13 oversight visits at ICE detention facilities in Arizona, Texas and Florida to witness firsthand the brutality and horrific conditions of these centers and hear from detainees firsthand.
She is a proud champion of the American Dream and Promise Act and believes we need to pass comprehensive immigration reform that will protect our diverse communities, including Dreamers (DACA recipients), refugees, and asylum seekers, to ensure that they have the necessary tools to succeed.
Yassamin is deeply alarmed by the rapid advancement of highly capable AI frontier technologies.
She is a proud supporter of legislation introduced by Congressman Greg Casar and Senator Bernie Sanders to ban artificial superintelligence, pause advanced AI research, and establish a new federal agency to regulate AI technologies and the AI industry.
She believes trillion-dollar AI companies are putting their record profits over the safety of the entire globe.
A champion of AI safety in the Congress, Yassamin has led the way in demanding that Trump convene an international effort to set global AI rules — as the U.S. has led in the past with nuclear and aviation safety.
She also knows that the Trump Administration’s refusal to regulate the AI industry — despite dire warnings about potential threats to the safety and economic well-being of Americans — is all part of the corruption story, with Donald Trump and his sons all profiting off of AI related investments.
Yassamin is leading the charge to impeach Pete Hegseth for incompetence, mismanagement, and crimes.
As a member of the powerful House Oversight Committee, she is investigating Jeffrey Epstein’s crimes and the biggest cover-up in American history, led by Donald Trump and his administration.
She is demanding answers on Trump family corruption, Big Oil’s pay-to-play, the administration’s violations of court orders, and its illegal dismantling of federal agencies, undermining public health, and the indiscriminate firing of government employees.
Yassamin does not take a single dime in corporate PAC money, and supports legislation to Abolish Super PACS to get big money out of politics .
Yassamin serves as the Ranking Member of the Energy and Mineral Resources Subcommittee of the House Natural Resources Committee, where she works tirelessly to hold Big Oil and corporate polluters accountable.
She deeply values our public lands and national monuments, and is committed to protecting them against attacks by congressional Republicans and the Trump administration.
Yassamin believes we must aggressively invest in clean energy projects and energy efficiency, electrify our transportation system, and ensure that we not only meet our climate and emissions commitments, but surpass them.
Yassamin supports halting the construction of more massive data centers until we have a comprehensive plan to protect our water, our electrical grid, and Arizona ratepayers.
She believes we must tackle our state’s historic water crisis and prioritize the people of Arizona first.
Yassamin believes in the power of multilateral institutions and negotiations through diplomacy. She started her career at the United Nations as an advisor on the Secretary-General’s Climate Action Team where she helped to deliver the historic Paris Climate Agreement.
She has been fighting for an end to Trump’s horrific and illegal war in Iran, including with accountability for unacceptable civilian deaths and potential war crimes in U.S. strikes in Minab, Iran.
She firmly believes that the administration’s actions in Cuba and the Caribbean are outrageous and immoral.
She is proud to stand with U.S. allies in NATO, for the sovereignty of other nations like Denmark and Canada, and to support Ukraine in its fight for freedom.
Yassamin knows that the only way to have lasting and enduring peace in the Middle East is for there to be an independent, viable, and prosperous Palestinian state alongside a secure Israel. She strongly opposes the Netanyahu government’s appalling actions in Gaza, Lebanon, and the West Bank which undermine that future, and she is a cosponsor of the Block the Bombs Act .
Yassamin believes gun violence is a national emergency and a public health epidemic. She is an original co-sponsor of the Stop Online Ammunition Sales Act of 2026 that would require federally licensed dealers to verify the identity of individuals purchasing ammunition online by checking a photo I.D.
She supported H. R. 1307, the Office of Gun Violence Prevention Act of 2025, a bill that would reestablish an Office of Gun Violence Prevention, which was dismantled by the Trump Administration.
Yassamin is a proud cosponsor of Medicare for All and believes healthcare is a human right.
She believes we must also address the glaring inequities in our healthcare system, which has historically ignored or downplayed the pain of women and people of color. That’s why Yassamin introduced the HER Agenda, which includes:
- The Gynecologic Pain Management Study Act, to address barriers to access for pain management options during gynecologic procedures.
- The Reproductive Healthcare Leave Act, to provide 12 days of paid leave for reproductive health reasons like extreme menstrual pain, menopause symptoms, vasectomies, and more.
- The Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder (PMDD) Research Act, to study under-researched and underdiagnosed PMDD, a severe form of PMS.
Yassamin believes that housing is a human right and that we must build more housing (and quickly!), invest massively in social housing projects, and expand support for low-income renters.
That’s why she introduced the HAVEN Act, which expands housing voucher programs to cover every eligible household, expands eligibility, and bans landlords from discriminating against voucher-holding tenants.
She was also proud to support and pass the bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act – the most significant housing legislation in decades.
Yassamin is a cosponsor of the John R Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act.
She is supportive of a House bill calling for restoring and strengthening the Voting Rights Act, eliminating the Senate filibuster, and enacting structural changes to the Supreme Court.
She supports the Youth Voting Rights Act that establishes a private right of action to enforce the Twenty-Sixth Amendment, which prohibits denying or abridging the right to vote based on age.
Yassamin proudly serves the men and women who have served in uniform. She co-sponsored the Major Richard Star Act to ensure that combat-injured veterans receive their full earned benefits.
She is a proud supporter of the Protect Veteran Jobs Act to reinstate veterans who were dismissed from federal employment without cause since President Trump took office.
She endorsed the Caring for Survivors Act that would increase monthly financial benefits and expand eligibility for the surviving spouses of our fallen veterans.
She supported the Veterans Infertility Treatment Act to make infertility care part of VA-provided health care benefits.
She strongly advocates for the Supporting VA Families Act that would guarantee unpaid parental leave for all employees of the Department of Veterans Affairs.

pages.title: Accomplishments - Yassamin for Congress
pages.text:
## accomplishments
In her first term in Congress, Yassamin focused on delivering real results for everyday Arizonans while working tirelessly to stand up against the corrupt and authoritarian Trump Administration. She hit the ground running and in less than two years:
Secured over $17.7 million in Community Project Funding for critical investments, including park reconstruction, public sanitation, public transportation and safety projects, homeless shelters, and community support programs, Arizona State University research initiatives, and more.
Led the Lowering Costs Task Force of the Congressional Progressive Caucus to pioneer innovative solutions to the affordability crisis. She hosted several listening tours across the United States to listen to Americans about the rising cost of living under the Trump Administration.
Introduced the historic Health, Equity, and Rights (HER) Agenda , a first-of-its-kind legislative package that addresses disparities in women’s healthcare. As the youngest woman in Congress, Yassamin knows the pain women suffer from in silence, focusing on investing federal dollars into pain management for gynecological procedures, implementing paid leave for symptoms related to reproductive health conditions, and funding clinical trials for PMDD, a severe form of premenstrual syndrome (PMS).
Introduced the Extreme Heat Agenda , a legislative package to address and mitigate the effects of extreme heat through expanded federal coordination, funding for local heat mitigation projects, and investments aimed at strengthening community preparedness for rising temperatures.
Fought at the forefront against ICE and Trump’s inhumane deportation agenda across the nation, calling to abolish ICE and hold the administration responsible.
- Yassamin was one of just four Members of Congress to travel to El Salvador to demand the release of Kilmar Abrego Garcia , who had been deported to CECOT prison without due process and held in El Salvador in violation of the Supreme Court’s ruling. After months of advocacy, Kilmar was returned to the United States.
- Conducted 12+ Congressional oversight visits to detention centers and holding facilities across Arizona, Texas, and Florida, including the Dilley Child Prison Camp. Yassamin’s advocacy has brought national attention to the cell overcrowding, abuse, and inhumane treatment that is taking place inside these taxpayer-funded facilities.
- Advocated for the release of her constituent Arbella “Yari” Rodriguez Marquez , a leukemia patient who has spent the last year at Eloy Detention Center without adequate medical treatment. Yari is a lawful resident of Arizona with no criminal record, facing severe medical neglect that has led to unnecessary health complications and suffering. The direct involvement of Yassamin’s team was crucial to securing Yari’s medical records and oncology appointments.
- Introduced the DRAIN ICE Act to repeal the $75 billion in funding for ICE designated by the “Big Beautiful Bill,” mandate reporting requirements for detainees including health conditions and deaths in custody, and study the long-term economic impacts of Trump’s immigration policies.
As a member of the powerful House Oversight Committee , Yassamin has been a leading voice in calling out Trump’s egregious cover-up of the Epstein Files. Yassamin has fought for justice, accountability, and transparency for the American people over the Epstein Files and Trump’s botched investigation, uplifting survivors’ stories and attending depositions with Howard Lutnick, Pam Bondi, Les Wexner, and more.
Called for the 25th Amendment for the removal of President Donald Trump and impeachment of Secretary of War Pete Hegseth from office over his illegal war with Iran that violates Article 1, Section 8 of the Constitution. As the first Iranian-American Democrat in Congress, Yassamin defended American servicemembers who were endangered by Trump and Hegseth’s recklessness, and the Iranian people’s right to protest against the Islamic Republic for a free, democratic future.
Introduced the HAVEN ACT , a housing affordability bill to cap rent for families on housing assistance to 20% of their income. The program expands housing voucher access for financial assistance, protects families from housing discrimination, and lowers outdated federal income standards to qualify for assistance.
Introduced legislation to ensure year-round access to affordable heating and cooling for low-income households. This expansion of the Low Income Housing Energy Assistance Program protects low-income families that often pay higher energy bills from utilizing outdated heating and cooling equipment, which is crucial to protect families from rising temperatures.
Passed bipartisan legislation in the House to develop standards for geothermal energy. Having spent her career working on climate action policy, her first passed bill ensures that geothermal investments are sustainable and safely regulated in the United States.
Attended the Munich Security Conference as a Freshman Member of Congress to unite with global leaders and call for transformative foreign policy change to protect people from the climate crisis and endless wars.

## Category: Policy
Glendale, Guadalupe, and Phoenix are on the front lines of climate change, extreme heat, and water scarcity, and it’s up to our generation of leaders to take bold action to save lives and ensure a safe and healthy quality life for the decades to come.
It is imperative that our leaders and elected officials work to ensure that the current rising cost of living for our working families goes down to ensure that we can provide economic stability and financial freedom.
In our first plan, we address the ways in which our minority-owned small businesses face barriers to their economic success, and the ways in which we can advocate for systemic change from the top down to ensure that everyone has access to the same resources.
Yassamin is dedicated to ensuring that we stop rolling back the clocks on reproductive healthcare, and enshrine it as a fundamental right once and for all.
Universal access to safe, stable,
and affordable housing is the cornerstone of a thriving community—one where everyone can live with dignity.
